newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ABC says union plans stopwork action.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ABC says union plans stopwork action.

text.p: The Australian Broadcasting Corp (ABC) said on Monday that the Commonwealth Public Sector Union (CPSU) had called for a national stopwork meeting on Tuesday over proposed government budget cuts to the broadcaster.

The government is also expected to make a decision on Tuesday over whether it will keep the Radio Australia and Australian Television International services, which are both directed at Asia. ABC management has advised its workers not to join in the union's planned industrial action, which could disrupt the broadcaster's radio and television operations.
The government plans to cut ABC funding by A$55 million.

The closure of both services was recommended in a government commissioned review of the state broadcaster, which also recommended that the ABC contract out its television production work and sell surplus land.

"The action of the CPSU undervalues the enormous effort of the board, management, staff and the union to deal with the huge task of reshaping the ABC against a background of government's proposed budget cuts of A$55 million to effectively maintain our role as a quality public broadcaster," ABC head of human resources Jacquie Hutchinson said in an ABC memo to staff.
